Compliance - Audit Team: Hey support, our compliance team can't view audit logs for org acme-corp. Getting 403 when hitting /v1/audit/logs. Need urgent — audit retention review pending. :exclamation:
Jen (support): Sorry to hear that. Can you paste the exact error payload you see and how you're calling the API? Also who/what identity is being used (API key vs SSO session)?
Compliance - Audit Team: We're using the org-level UI (Console) and the audit export API from our internal job which uses our OIDC app token. Repro steps:
1) Sign in to Console as alice@acme (SSO) -> Navigate to Admin > Audit logs -> UI shows "You do not have permission to view audit logs"
2) Run curl:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -X GET "https://api.redwood.example/v1/audit/logs?org=acme-corp"
```
Response:
```json
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "entitlement_required",
  "message": "missing:audits.read_retention",
  "details": {
    "entitlement": "audit_read_retention",
    "subject": "alice@acme"
  }
}
```
Jen (support): Thanks, that error string is helpful. Two likely vectors: entitlement/role not present on the user or OIDC token missing expected claims that map to Redwood entitlements. Are you on OIDC with custom claim mapping?
Compliance - Audit Team: Yes, Okta. We recently rolled a change to claim mapping (shrunk token claims to reduce size). Could that have dropped something?
Devon H: That aligns. We recently added guardrails to reject requests where retention-specific entitlements are missing for audit views. The UI checks both "audit:read" and "audit:read_retention" entitlements. If the id_token or user profile lacks the SCIM group that maps to retention entitlement, you'll hit 403.
Priya K: Can you grab the introspection of the token or the id_token payload (JWT) for alice? Specifically we want to see "scp", "entitlements", and any groups claim. Example introspect:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://idp.okta/acme/oauth2/v1/introspect" \\
  -d "token=$TOKEN" -u client_id:client_secret
```
Or decode the id_token: `echo $ID_TOKEN | cut -d'.' -f2 | base64 -d`
Compliance - Audit Team: Pasted decoded id_token (sanitized):
```json
{
  "sub": "00u1abcd...",
  "email": "alice@acme",
  "scp": "openid profile email",
  "groups": ["engineering", "admins"],
  "auth_time": 1670000000
}
```
Jen (support): I see `scp` has no `audit:read` scopes and there's no `entitlements` claim. That explains it. The token is missing both the explicit audit scope and the entitlement mapping.
Eli S: Quick workaround: grant alice a temporary org role via console (Org Admin) or add a scoped service token to the automation job. But for SSO users we should fix claim mapping in Okta so new tokens include the `entitlements` claim.
Compliance - Audit Team: We don't want to make everyone Org Admin. Can we grant just the audit retention entitlement?
Devon H: Yes — two options:
1) SCIM group sync: map an Okta group (e.g., `acme-audit-read-retention`) -> SCIM group -> Redwood entitlement `audit_read_retention`. Once SCIM sync runs, the user will get the entitlement on next login.
2) OIDC claim mapping: add a custom claim in Okta that aggregates group membership into an `entitlements` array and map that to Redwood's entitlement names. Example claim config:
```json
{"name":"entitlements","include_in_tokens":["id_token","access_token"],"value":"groups.map(g => g == 'acme-audit-read' ? 'audit_read_retention' : null).filter(x=>x)"}
```
Priya K: Also note retention entitlements are handled separately from `audit:read`. You need both `audit:read` (view) and `audit_read_retention` (see retention/exports). The UI will surface different CTAs depending on entitlements.
Compliance - Audit Team: Okta admin says they removed a claim last week. We'll re-add the claim and force a re-login. Any API checks to verify entitlements have landed?
Jen (support): Once IdP change is made, have the user sign out/sign in. To verify from our side you can call the users endpoint and check entitlements returned by Redwood (requires a support/admin token). Example (support only):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPPORT_TOKEN" \\n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/orgs/acme-corp/users/alice@acme
```
Response expected snippet:
```json
{
  "email": "alice@acme",
  "entitlements": ["audit:read","audit_read_retention"]
}
```
Devon H: If customers can't change IdP fast enough, we can offer a temporary org-level entitlement grant (support action). Jen, can you confirm process and TTL for emergency grants?
Jen (support): We have a documented emergency grant process (see internal runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/support/emergency-entitlements). We can do a 24h grant scoped to `audit_read_retention` for a named user after SOC approval. Need requestor email + reason.
SRE Bot: Incident created: INC-2026 - audit log view blocked for acme-corp (priority P2). Assign: DevOps oncall.
Compliance - Audit Team: Okta claim restored, user re-logged in. Still getting 403 on export job (headless automation). Token decode now shows:
```json
{
  "email": "svc-exports@acme",
  "scp": "audit:read api:export",
  "entitlements": ["audit:read","audit_read_retention"],
  "client_id": "svc-exports-client"
}
```
Jen (support): Good. If the service client now has entitlements but still fails, check that the service client is allowed in Redwood to use retention exports (some orgs have policy requiring human user confirmation). Can you paste the exact 403 body from the job?
Compliance - Audit Team: Now showing: `403 {"error":"org_policy_block","message":"service_clients_require_export_whitelist"}`
Priya K: That's org policy. For automation, the client_id must be on the org's export whitelist. We can add it via admin API if you're an Org Admin, or we can do it for you after verification. Curl (Org Admin):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/orgs/acme-corp/policy/export-whitelist \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ORG_ADMIN_TOKEN" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"client_id":"svc-exports-client","expires_in":86400}'
```
Compliance - Audit Team: We don't have an Org Admin on call. Can support apply the whitelist temporarily?
Jen (support): Yes, we'll initiate emergency grant flow. Please DM me the service client_id and approval email. I'll create a 24h whitelist entry and confirm.
Devon H: Long term action items I'll take:
- Update docs to clearly differentiate `audit:read` vs `audit_read_retention` entitlements.
- Add validation to error message to recommend IdP claim troubleshooting (link to runbook).
- Add telemetry to detect sudden claim removals so we can proactively notify customers.
Compliance - Audit Team: Thx all. One ask: can we get a quick note we can send to Okta folks showing exactly the claim mapping snippet we need?
Priya K: Copy-paste this to them:
```text
Create a custom claim named `entitlements` in Okta. Include in ID and access tokens. Value should map Okta group names to Redwood entitlement strings, e.g.:
- groups contains `acme-audit-read` -> `audit:read`
- groups contains `acme-audit-retention` -> `audit_read_retention`

Ensure SCIM group sync is configured so membership updates reflect in Redwood. After changes, have users re-login and re-run the export job.
```
Jen (support): All set — I've filed INC-2026 with the emergency whitelist request and provisioned a 24h whitelist for `svc-exports-client` pending SOC verify. Closing once acme confirms export succeeded. :white_check_mark:
Compliance - Audit Team: Export job completed successfully after whitelist. Thanks everyone.
Jen (support): Marking resolved in thread, will follow up with postmortem doc and docs PR for claim troubleshooting.
